title: kbmon --split opens the live view in a WezTerm, tmux or Windows Terminal pane beside the session
goal: kbmon.py --split opens the live view (kbmon.py --interval 60) in a pane beside the session: wezterm cli split-pane where WEZTERM_PANE is set, tmux split-window where TMUX is set, Windows Terminal split-pane where WT_SESSION is set; elsewhere it prints the command to run in a second terminal and names the optional WezTerm installer; --dry-run prints the command it would run; it exits 0 in every case; the split pane's live view adds no constant CPU load (operator, 2026-10-19): 30 s of kbmon.py --interval 60 cost under 6 CPU seconds

clauses.clause: kbmon.py --split opens the live view (kbmon.py --interval 60) in a pane beside the session: wezterm cli split-pane where WEZTERM_PANE is set, tmux split-window where TMUX is set, Windows Terminal split-pane where WT_SESSION is set
elsewhere it prints the command to run in a second terminal and names the optional WezTerm installer
--dry-run prints the command it would run
the split pane's live view adds no constant CPU load (operator, 2026-10-19): 30 s of kbmon.py --interval 60 cost under 6 CPU seconds

gates.question: When more than one of TMUX, WEZTERM_PANE and WT_SESSION is set (tmux inside WezTerm), which terminal does --split use?
options: tmux first, then WezTerm, then Windows Terminal
WezTerm first, then tmux, then Windows Terminal
gates.recommendation: tmux first, then WezTerm, then Windows Terminal
gates.answer: tmux first, then WezTerm, then Windows Terminal

gates.question: How wide is the split pane, and which options of the --split run does its live view take along?
options: 40 percent of the width; --root, --panel, --store, --url and --key-file go along
40 percent of the width; no option goes along
gates.recommendation: 40 percent of the width; --root, --panel, --store, --url and --key-file go along
gates.answer: 40 percent of the width; --root, --panel, --store, --url and --key-file go along

gates.question: When the splitting command is missing or fails, or no terminal is detected, what does --split do?
options: print the command for a second terminal with the WezTerm installer hint, say why on stderr, exit 0
gates.recommendation: print the command for a second terminal with the WezTerm installer hint, say why on stderr, exit 0
gates.answer: print the command for a second terminal with the WezTerm installer hint, say why on stderr, exit 0

notes: Plan 2026-10-19: premise on the base: kbmon.py has no --split (exit 2). Prototype: a tmux split-window -d -h -l 45% opened the live view from a SessionStart hook and redrew at once on a resize. wezterm cli split-pane --right --percent N --cwd DIR -- PROG targets WEZTERM_PANE (vendor docs wezterm.org/cli/cli/split-pane.html, 2026-10-19, not in the kb yet); Windows Terminal wt -w 0 split-pane -V -d DIR commandline (learn.microsoft.com/windows/terminal/command-line-arguments, 2026-10-19). Apple Terminal has no split command: the hint path. --interval 60 keeps the live view's CPU low until ST-5bz4nwsf.
